prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks based on magic-wavelength trapping, bringing frequency measurement to the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: I keep B014 as my preferred configuration, unchanged from round 1, and I have tested it against the chair's own questions. The achievement is a single identifiable invention: trapping many atoms at a magic wavelength so that the light shift cancels, and interrogating a narrow clock transition with them at once. That removed the limit of single-ion and free-fall clocks and carried optical clocks to about 10^-18, confirmed in several laboratories, species and clock-to-clock comparisons. The consequences are concrete: the redefinition of the second, centimetre-level relativistic geodesy, tests of constant variation and dark-matter searches. Attribution is the firmest on the shortlist: Katori's proposal and first realization, Ye's record accuracy and many-body clock programme, two names that leave one name of headroom and no obvious gap in the core. On the question I put to the room, I would decide between B014 and B016 first on clarity of credit and a closed, reproduced result, and second on conceptual breadth. B016 wins on breadth, but it fails my credit test more severely. The citation I propose names magic-wavelength trapping and the accuracy it allowed, so it cannot be read as a second prize for optical frequency metrology in general. I am not moved by the count of supporters, which the chair summary also warns against. I note that B014 and B016 are both mature and that I would accept a B016 outcome if the committee judged the Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang omission defensible.
statement.case_against: The strongest argument against is that precision timekeeping has been honoured in 2005 (Hall and Haensch, the comb) and 2012 (Wineland, ion control), and that the lattice clock may be read as an extraordinary refinement of that line rather than a discovery. I regard the magic wavelength as an independent idea, but the point is a fair one and Danielsson and Johansson both press it. Second, the SI second has not been redefined, so one could wait; I do not think the redefinition is a scientific criterion, but a majority may weigh timing differently. Third, the claims of Lemonde, Ludlow, Takamoto, Lemke, the ion-clock groups and the PTB, Paris and NIST teams remain outside the two names, and I have not verified chronology against the nomination files. Finally, a prize in metrology is easy to call less transformative than a new classification of electronic phases, which is the heart of the B016 case.

responses.point: Kroll asks the chair whether his doctoral time in Hall's Boulder laboratory, in the same environment as Ye's group, calls for recusal or disclosure only on B014, and he keeps B014 first.
responses.response: As chair I would treat this as disclosure, not recusal: a doctoral period in a neighbouring laboratory, with no recorded collaboration with Katori or Ye and no shared publications or funding, is the ordinary scientific proximity the committee already accepts (I make the same disclosure for IceCube, in my own field). I would record the disclosure in the minutes and let it stand unless the committee finds a specific tie. I also keep the narrower point from round 1: his claim that the 2005 comb prize does not crowd out B014 is right only if the citation is anchored on magic-wavelength trapping, since the comb is the readout of these clocks.

responses.point: Danielsson holds B016 first as the most conceptually original chain, says the 2016 overlap is distinct, and accepts that B014 is the better-attributed candidate and a strong alternative.
responses.response: His acknowledgement that B014 is better attributed is the point that decides it for me. I agree that Z2 time-reversal-invariant insulators are separate from the 2016 Chern-insulator physics, and I have dropped that as an objection to B016. What I cannot dismiss is that the HgTe route came from Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and that Zhang's death makes the gap permanent. His own uncertainty list says that the omission could make the prize incomplete. If conceptual breadth is the first criterion, he is right to prefer B016; I put weight on credit that can be defended in a citation, and on that criterion B014 is stronger. I would not oppose B016 if the committee decides the omission can be justified.

responses.point: Johansson says B014 is her honest second choice and would be the cleaner two-person allocation if the HgTe attribution cannot be defended, but she thinks the lattice clock rewards metrological performance more than a new physical effect.
responses.response: Her conditional is helpful because it names the exact test: can the committee defend the HgTe attribution? I do not think it can without leaving a real gap. On her performance-versus-new-effect objection, I think the cancellation of the differential light shift at a magic wavelength is a new physical effect, which exists only because of the atomic-structure insight and is not an engineering refinement of the comb. The accuracy followed from it, not the other way around. I also take her imperfect-quantization remark in longer HgTe channels as a real weakness of the experimental half of B016, which narrows the gap in confirmation between the two candidates.

responses.point: Olsson has moved to B014 from B042 and flags a possible institutional link to Katori through her Tokyo fellowship and Japanese exchanges, which she has not yet checked, and she notes that B042 omits the Krivanek work.
responses.response: I welcome that she did not wait for the chair's question and disclosed the Tokyo link. I would ask her to establish before the vote whether it is a tie to Katori's own institution; a general exchange with Japanese universities is only disclosure, whereas a current affiliation or joint project would be a recusal question. I agree with her reading of B042: the omission of the scanning-transmission corrector work makes the credit set incomplete, so I am comfortable that it stays an alternative for her and I have not included it among mine.

responses.point: Mehlig moved from B001 to B016 after reading the ballots, argues that Z2 insulators are distinct from the 2016 prize, and also lists B014 as his alternative with a fair two-person attribution.
responses.response: His move seems to rest on substance and not on counts, and I agree that the 2016 point does not defeat B016. His own case against, however, names the incomplete credit, the passing of Zhang and imperfect HgTe quantization, and each of those counts against the experimental half, which is what makes B016 a discovery in nature. The B016 and B014 choice therefore comes down to whether the committee weighs breadth over clean credit. I would put the same question back to him: if the committee could not widen the credit beyond three names, would he accept B014 as the defensible choice?

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts the lattice clock as a discovery or invention distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, which is the central unresolved scientific dispute in the first round.
Whether to wait for the formal redefinition of the SI second. I treat it as a supporting application, but I cannot show that others should do the same.
The relative weight of Katori and Ye, and the strength of the claims of Lemonde, Ludlow, Takamoto, Lemke and the ion-clock groups; chronology is recalled, not verified against the nominations.
Whether I weigh clean attribution too heavily over conceptual breadth, since that choice decides between B014 and B016 and is a judgment, not a measurement.

My alternatives B016 and B021 are held on different grounds: B016 as a mature but incompletely credited result, and B021 where source identification and the allocation inside the IceCube collaboration remain unsettled.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict is recorded for B014: my documented connections (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur) involve none of the credited names. As chair I record that I find Kroll's Boulder connection to be a disclosure matter and not recusal, and that Olsson's Japanese link should be checked and reported before the vote. B021 (IceCube) lies in my own field of astroparticle physics with no recorded tie to Halzen, Karle or Spiering; I flag that proximity because it is one of my alternatives.
